My detailed review of DG RUPAREL college

Campus(4.5/5): It's a pretty good campus as the ground is good but gets worse during rainy season so be careful of that . A volleyball court which is good too. Pretty good greenery all over the campus.

Other than that the ground for playing and all yes you can play on the ground only after you get your id card and have to ask in the office if playing on ground is allowed or not just to be on the safer side the timings for that are 3-6 only in the afternoon(if you are not from the college sports team for those students) . Boards perspective (4/5): Teachers manage your marks in the internals help you during practicals and if you manage to stay in their good looks you'll get out of marks in the internals just attend the practicals and clear all the submissions on time

Overall(3/5): a decent college if you want stress free attendance and internals during boards etc but if you want to live your college life like in the movies plzzz don't come in this college

The university operates primarily from two campuses: the Fort Campus, known for its historic Rajabai Clock Tower, and the expansive Kalina Campus, which spans 243 acres and provides a serene environment conducive to learning and research.  ￼

Students have access to comprehensive facilities, including separate hostels for boys and girls, well-furnished rooms, spacious classrooms, and full-time internet connectivity.  The Jawaharlal Nehru Library serves as a central resource, housing an extensive collection of academic materials.  ￼ ￼

The university has produced notable alumni who have significantly contributed to various fields. However, some students have expressed concerns regarding placement opportunities, citing limited campus recruitment and lower salary packages.  Despite these challenges, the University of Mumbai remains a prominent educational institution, blending historical significance with academic diversity. ￼
